event.marcus_heart2.1.text: Measure once. Twice. ...Three times. Three times. Easy, now. Rest your end on the bench.
event.marcus_heart2.1.why: Frightened: the count stammers (short repeat) and he takes the weight off the player's shaking hands.

event.marcus_heart2.1.text: Measure once. Twice. ...Three times, my father said. You look short on sleep. Holding helps.
event.marcus_heart2.1.why: Uneasy: he notices the player's tiredness and gives them a job, the Keeper's gentleness.

event.marcus_heart2.2.text: Take these. Leftovers from the big jobs. Go home with them now, friend. Before the light goes.
event.marcus_heart2.2.why: Frightened: the gift becomes a reason to send the player home before dark; care that is too exact.

event.marcus_heart5.4.text: Edmund's cellar door. He wouldn't let me oil it. He wanted to hear us coming, at the end.
event.marcus_heart5.4.why: Revelation: 'us' and 'at the end' let slip that the Keepers came for Edmund, without a single ritual word.

event.marcus_heart5.4.text: Edmund had a door that never opened. His cellar. He wouldn't let me oil it. ...Don't you oil it either.
event.marcus_heart5.4.why: Frightened: a protective instruction the player cannot yet explain; sends them to the cellar door.

event.marcus_heart5.4.text: Edmund's cellar door. He wouldn't let me oil it. A door that squeaks tells you who's keeping watch.
event.marcus_heart5.4.why: Clue: 'keeping watch' names a duty and ties Edmund to it.

event.marcus_heart5.4.text: Edmund had a door that never opened. His cellar. He wouldn't let me oil it. If it squeaks at night, that's the cold.
event.marcus_heart5.4.why: Uneasy: a kind cover that tells the player the door squeaks at night.

event.marcus_heart5.2.text: Keep your tools sharp, friend. The bag is for your fields. And keep a lamp lit. Humor me.
event.marcus_heart5.2.why: Frightened: he trades the joke for a lamp, echoing Tilda's; gentler, which frightens more.

event.hall_dance.0.text: I checked the roof once. Twice. Three. Three times. It is finished. It will hold. Whatever comes.
event.hall_dance.0.why: Frightened: the count slips and 'whatever comes' makes the roof a shelter, not a project.

event.hall_dance.0.text: I checked the roof three times. It is finished. One thing in this village I don't have to keep watch over.
event.hall_dance.0.why: Clue: there are other things he keeps watch over.

event.hall_dance.0.text: I checked the roof once. Twice. ...Three times. It is finished. Stay until the lamps go out. Everyone's here.
event.hall_dance.0.why: Uneasy: 'everyone's here' is a headcount; the Keeper is relieved the whole village is under one roof.

event.hall_dance.11.text: The ladder can wait one night. One dance. Then I walk you home. Not alone tonight.
event.hall_dance.11.why: Frightened: the Keeper's tell, 'not alone after dark', in the happiest scene of his arc.

event.story_pie_payoff.intro.text: [player]. A word, quietly. You know the way to the clinic? The lit road, mind. Not the wood path.
event.story_pie_payoff.intro.why: Uneasy: an exact route for a short errand; names the wood path as something to avoid.

dlg.story.pie.talk.0.text: One slice of my pie. Her door. No name. She carries more than she lets on. Pie helps.
dlg.story.pie.talk.0.why: Clue: Dr. Penn carries a weight; points the player at the Keepers' leader.

dlg.story.pie.talk.1.text: Well? You can say no. You look like you need a slice yourself. Take two.
dlg.story.pie.talk.1.why: Frightened: the joke softens into feeding the player.

event.story_whistler_marcus.intro.text: Ah. You've found me. I whistle so you know where I am. You should be home. I'll walk you.
event.story_whistler_marcus.intro.why: Frightened: the whistle becomes a signal in the dark; he escorts.

event.story_whistler_marcus.intro.text: Ah. You've found me. I whistle when the grain runs true. Also after dark. Keeps the evening friendly.
event.story_whistler_marcus.intro.why: Uneasy: whistling to keep the dark at bay.

dlg.story.whistler.marcus.0.text: It's an old Wetherell tune. Four notes. My grandfather hit one wrong. On purpose, I think now.
dlg.story.whistler.marcus.0.why: Clue: echoes Edmund's four notes; a wrong note kept deliberately is a question to chase (Piper).

event.story_pumpkin_marcus.intro.text: You've caught me. A practice lantern. Lanterns want faces this time of year. I never asked whose pumpkin.
event.story_pumpkin_marcus.intro.why: Uneasy: a lit face for the dark as a village habit, ties to lamps lit early.

event.story_pumpkin_marcus.after.text: It goes back with a face carved in. Tilda will light it on her step. She keeps a lamp for everyone.
event.story_pumpkin_marcus.after.why: Clue: Tilda's lamp is a watch, not a habit.

event.marcus_heart8.intro.text: Come in. Sit by the stove first. You've seen the barn I carved at nine. Now see the roof plan.
event.marcus_heart8.intro.why: Frightened: warmth before business; the player is visibly shaken.

dlg.marcus.roof.1.text: Six winters, nearly fixed. Some things you never finish. You only keep them asleep. ...What would you do?
dlg.marcus.roof.1.why: Revelation: the roof talk slides into what the Keepers keep asleep, then he covers by asking about the roof.

dlg.marcus.roof.1.text: Six winters, nearly fixed. I keep other things longer than that. Heavier, too. ...What would you do?
dlg.marcus.roof.1.why: Clue: a duty he has kept for years.

dlg.marcus.roof.0.text: Pitch, rafters, shingles. Drawn nine times. Every time it looks right. Every time I'm afraid it won't hold. You know the feeling.
dlg.marcus.roof.0.why: Uneasy: he recognizes the player's fear as his own.

event.marcus_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. I planed a plank for it, like every year. Sit, if you like. You look like you need sitting.

dlg.marcus.birthday.r0.text: Thank you. I'll write that on the beam, small. Edmund's name is up there too. Same size.
dlg.marcus.birthday.r0.why: Clue: a beam of names, Edmund's among them, quietly memorialized.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_1.l3.text: Straight. That's the whole job. Like your counting. You never skip one.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_1.l3.why: Clue: Marcus knows Dorian counts (the trees); two Keepers sharing a duty in a plank.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_2.l3.text: You came in late again. I nearly got worried. Then I didn't. Best hour of the week.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_2.l3.why: Hint: Dorian keeps late hours, and Marcus waits up.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_3.l3.text: That's all a door is for. Closing on purpose. Bar it on the fourth night.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_3.l3.why: Clue: names the new-moon night (day 4); Dorian's 'I'll leave it open' turns uneasy.

event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l3.text: Facing the owl, and the trees behind it. You can count them from bed now.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l3.why: Clue: echoes Dorian counting the trees; the window watches the wood.

event.overheard_bram_marcus_1.l4.text: Good. Hand me the clamp. Wednesday, same bench. Unless it's the fourth. Then I'm early to bed.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_1.l4.why: Hint: a Keeper excusing himself from the day-4 evening to an unaware friend.

event.overheard_marcus_odalys_2.l3.text: That's why it worked loose. You carry this whole village, Doctor. Five minutes would do it good.
event.overheard_marcus_odalys_2.l3.why: Clue: he names the weight Penn carries; care too exact.

event.overheard_marcus_odalys_3.l2.text: Better. I rest it Wednesdays. And after the new moon. The doctor told me to.
event.overheard_marcus_odalys_3.l2.why: Hint: the new moon is hard on his back, and the doctor knows why.

adds.text: One more thing. Home before dark on the new moon. My father's rule. Now it's mine.
adds.why: Hint-tier custom, passed on as a carpenter passes on a rule.

adds.text: ...Glued shut. Good. Some doors should stay that way.
adds.why: He checks the toy's shut doors after mentioning the cellar; points back at Edmund's door.

adds.text: ...Everyone under one roof. Good. I counted.
adds.why: The Keeper's headcount; makes the player wonder who he worries is missing.

adds.text: Getting dark. I'll whistle you as far as the store. Tilda's lamp takes it from there.
adds.why: Hint: Keepers hand the player along in the dark, one to the next.

cuts.why: 'Yours stayed put' is false (and unkind) when the player's hands shake; the frightened variant of .1 already took the weight.

threads.marcus_heart2: Why does Marcus keep a rule about the new moon, and whose rule was it first?
threads.marcus_heart5: What did Edmund want to hear through a door that squeaked?
threads.hall_dance: If one roof is the thing Marcus need not watch, what does he watch the rest of the time?
threads.story_pie_payoff: What does Dr. Penn carry that a slice of pie is meant to ease?
threads.story_whistler_marcus: Why does a family tune keep a wrong note on purpose, and why does it sound like Edmund's?
threads.story_pumpkin_marcus: Why does every doorstep want a lit face this time of year?
threads.marcus_heart8: What has Marcus kept longer and heavier than a roof?
threads.marcus_birthday: Why is Edmund's name on Marcus's beam?
threads.overheard_marcus_dorian_1: What is Dorian counting, and why must he never skip one?
threads.overheard_marcus_dorian_2: Where does Dorian go that he comes home late?
threads.overheard_marcus_dorian_3: What happens on the fourth night that a door should be barred?
threads.overheard_marcus_dorian_4: Why does Dorian need to see the trees from his bed?
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_1: Why does Marcus go to bed early on the fourth, when Bram doesn't?
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_2: None: left plain on purpose, a quiet scene for contrast.
threads.overheard_bram_marcus_3: None: left plain on purpose, a comic scene for contrast.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_1: None: left plain on purpose; the knees joke stays a joke.
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_2: What is the whole village that the doctor carries?
threads.overheard_marcus_odalys_3: What does the new moon do to Marcus's back?

notes: Cut of event.marcus_heart2.3 pairs with the frightened variant of event.marcus_heart2.1; keep them together.
Left the {if}-branched .after lines (pie, roof, birthday) and all choice labels untouched to preserve branching and choice meaning.
heart5 revelation variant implies the Keepers came for Edmund; full-only, no ritual words.
